tour.name: Grand Canyon South Rim Private Day Trip from Las Vegas: the Hoover Dam & Route 66
tour.subtitle: A private day to the most spectacular rim of the Grand Canyon with a local guide and vehicle: the Hoover Dam, a stop on Historic Route 66, the viewpoints of Mather Point, Yavapai and Desert View, a rim walk and the sunset at Hopi Point.

tour.overview:
The Grand Canyon of the Colorado River is some 446 kilometres long, up to 29 kilometres wide and more than 1,800 metres deep, and its walls expose nearly two billion years of the Earth's history in bands of red, orange and cream. It became a national park in 1919 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979. The South Rim, open all year, has the most famous viewpoints.

This private day trip takes you from Las Vegas to the South Rim and back with a local guide and a vehicle, about four and a half hours each way, via the Hoover Dam and Route 66, with time for the viewpoints, a rim walk and the sunset.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 15 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Las Vegas
• Type: private tour with local guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Hoover Dam.
• Route 66 at Seligman or Williams.
• Mather Point and the Yavapai Geology Museum.
• The Rim Trail.
• The Desert View Watchtower and sunset.

WHY THIS WORKS
The South Rim is much more spectacular than the West Rim; a private vehicle makes the long drive comfortable and flexible.

WHO IT SUITS
Nature lovers, photographers and families.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
To avoid the long drive, ask us to add a night at the canyon, or a helicopter or plane flight.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The South Rim is at about 2,100 metres and much cooler than Las Vegas; it can snow in winter. Arizona does not use daylight saving time.

days.name: The Hoover Dam, Route 66, the South Rim viewpoints and sunset
days.description:
What to expect: the drive across the Mojave and the great viewpoints of the South Rim, with a local guide, private vehicle, park fees and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 6:00 and drive south-east to the Hoover Dam, a concrete arch-gravity dam 221 metres high built in the 1930s on the Colorado River, on the border of Nevada and Arizona, seen from the bridge that crosses the gorge beside it. You continue across the Mojave Desert, with a stop on Historic Route 66 at Seligman or Williams, a small town of neon signs and old diners.

At the South Rim, your first view is from Mather Point, where the canyon opens suddenly at your feet. After lunch, you walk part of the Rim Trail to the Yavapai Geology Museum, where windows frame the canyon and exhibits explain how its layers formed. You drive the Desert View road, with stops at Grandview and Moran Points, to the Desert View Watchtower, built in 1932 by the architect Mary Colter with Hopi-inspired murals inside, overlooking a great bend of the Colorado River.

You end with the sunset at Hopi Point or Yaki Point, when the walls glow red and purple, and drive back to Las Vegas, arriving at about 22:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
06:00 – Pick-up in Las Vegas.
06:45 – Hoover Dam.
09:30 – Route 66.
11:30 – Mather Point.
12:15 – Lunch.
13:00 – Rim Trail and Yavapai.
14:30 – Desert View road and Watchtower.
Sunset – Hopi or Yaki Point.
22:30 – Back in Las Vegas.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A helicopter flight from Tusayan can be added.
• In winter, sunset is early and the day ends earlier.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, local guide, park entrance, lunch, water and snacks, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: helicopter flight, dinner, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How long is the drive?
faq.answer: About 4 hours 30 minutes each way. It is a long day, with stops to break it up.

faq.question: Why the South Rim and not the West Rim?
faq.answer: The South Rim, in the national park, has the most famous and spectacular views. The West Rim, with the Skywalk, is closer but less impressive.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a picnic or a lunch at the canyon.

faq.question: Can we stay overnight?
faq.answer: Yes. A night at the canyon lets you see sunrise too; lodges book up early.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children who can manage a long day. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. Many viewpoints are close to parking and the Rim Trail is paved.

faq.question: Can we hike into the canyon?
faq.answer: A short walk down the Bright Angel or South Kaibab trail is possible; never try to reach the river and back in a day.

faq.question: Can we add a flight?
faq.answer: Yes, a helicopter flight over the canyon from Tusayan.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Layers, a warm jacket in winter, comfortable shoes, a hat and sun cream.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: March to May and September to November. Summer is busy but fine at the rim.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in the United States: 15 to 20 percent is usual for guides and drivers if you were happy with the service, but it is always your choice.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
